text: To Sardis: he who holds the seven spirits and stars says they seem alive but are dead.
They must wake up and strengthen what is left.
They must recall what they received, keep it, and repent, or he will come like a thief.
Yet a few there have not soiled their clothes and will walk with him in white.
The conqueror will be dressed in white and his name kept in the book of life.
Whoever has ears should hear.
To Philadelphia: the holy and true one with the key of David speaks.
He has set an open door before them, though their strength is small and they kept his word.
He will make some opponents come and bow at their feet.
Because they endured, he will keep them in the coming hour of testing.
He is coming soon, so they should hold on to their crown.
The conqueror will be a pillar in God's temple, marked with God's name.
Whoever has ears should hear.
To Laodicea: the faithful and true witness speaks.
He knows their deeds: they are neither cold nor hot.
Being lukewarm, they will be spat out.
They boast of wealth, but are really wretched, poor, blind and naked.
He advises buying refined gold, white clothes and eye salve from him.
He disciplines those he loves, so they should be earnest and repent.
He stands at the door knocking, and will share a meal with anyone who opens.
The conqueror will sit with him on his throne.
Whoever has ears should hear.
